title: Sri Dvaraka Krishna, Sri Rukmini, the Sacred Tree and Goshala
summary: Sri Krishna, who came from Dvaraka to Udupi, is enshrined here with Sri Rukmini, a sacred parijata tree and the Sri Krishna Raghavendra Goshala.
body:
Sri Krishna came from Dvaraka to Udupi within a lump of gopichandana, to bestow grace on Acharya Madhva and, through him, on us all. While digging a well in the northeast corner before this shrine, the earth at a certain depth resembled gopichandana. Sri Vidyadhisha Tirtha Swamiji of Udupi Palimaru Matha therefore consecrated Sri Dvaraka Krishna on 9 February 2017. Devotees relate that tying a coconut here and worshipping for forty-eight days at this Dakshina Dvaraka shrine helps bring cherished prayers to fulfilment.

Sri Krishna Paramatma brought the heavenly parijata tree to earth, so a parijata behind the shrine serves as the sacred sthala-vriksha. Since Krishna brought it for Sri Rukmini, her shrine stands close beside his.

Granthalaya also houses the Sri Krishna Raghavendra Goshala. Contributions are welcomed for cow protection, annadana and construction.
images: SRI DVARAKA KRISHNA and SRI RUKMINI.jpg

title: Sri Manchalamma and Sri Mangadu Amman
summary: As at Mantralayam, devotees first seek the darshana of Sri Manchalamma and Mangadu Sri Kamakshi Amman before ascending to Sri Raghavendra.
body: It is customary at Mantralayam to seek the darshana of Sri Manchalamma before that of Sri Raghavendra. Likewise, here devotees first worship Manchalamma and Mangadu Sri Kamakshi Amman, whose shrine in the northeastern direction contains the Ardha Meru Sri Chakra. Then they ascend for Sri Raghavendra's darshana. Sri Dvaraka Krishna is to be worshipped before entering, with a reverent salutation and circumambulation of his shrine.

title: Sri Venkataramana, Sri Vyasa Hanuman and the Amrita-Hasta Brindavana
summary: The family deity Sri Prasanna Varada Venkataramana, Sri Vyasa Hanuman from Penukonda and a Brindavana holding mrttika given by Sri Raghavendra's own hands.
body:
Just as Sri Raghavendra consecrated his family deity Sri Venkataramana at Mantralayam, Sri Hari has come from Tirupati to preside here as Sri Prasanna Varada Venkataramana.

As Sri Vyasaraja, Sri Raghavendra fashioned, worshipped and bestowed 732 images of Anjaneya, beginning with the Yantroddharaka Hanuman of Hampi. The Hanuman here was brought from Penukonda, where 365 such images were consecrated, one for each day of the year.

This Brindavana is two inches shorter than the original at Mantralayam and is not carved from a single stone: thirty-two separately carved sections were lifted by crane and joined. Within it are hundreds of salagramas from Nepal's Gandaki River. Most uniquely, it enshrines sacred mrttika that Sri Raghavendra Himself gave to a disciple with His blessed hands. It was consecrated on 9 February 2017, and two sculpted goat heads stand before it, as at Mantralayam.
images: SRI VENKATARAMANA - SRI VYASA HANUMAN - SRI RAGHAVENDRA AMRITA-HASTA BRINDAVANA.jpg

title: Sri Mula Rama, Sri Rama Hanuman and the Four-Avatara Brindavana
summary: Three Rama images evoke the Tungabhadra's bank, a Hanuman carved from stone of Sri Rama's resting place, and a Brindavana of four incarnations.
body:
Tradition holds that Sri Raghavendra still bathes each dawn in the Tungabhadra at Mantralayam and worships Sri Mula Rama, Sri Digvijaya Rama and Sri Jaya Rama. The three Rama images are consecrated near the Brindavana here, evoking the river's bank.

While searching for Sita Devi, Sri Rama is believed to have rested on small rocks near Madhavaram, adjoining Mantralayam. The Mantralayam Brindavana was built on one such stone. A sacred stone brought from that place was fashioned into the seated Hanuman consecrated at Granthalaya.

Shankukarna of Brahmaloka descended as Prahlada, King Bahlika, Sri Vyasaraja and Sri Raghavendra. The small Brindavana presenting these four incarnations contains mrttika gifted by six yatis. Two mrttika Brindavanas, one large and one small, occupy the same sanctum, a distinctive feature of Granthalaya.
images: SRI MULA RAMA - SRI RAMA HANUMAN - FOUR-AVATARA BRINDAVANA.jpg

title: Gopuram Circumambulation and the Dvaraka Flag
summary: The four-sided vision of Sri Vijayadasa is reproduced on the gopuram, which devotees may circumambulate beneath the Dvaraka flag.
body:
Sri Vijayadasa (1682-1755) once visited Mantralayam and saw, above Sri Raghavendra's Mula Brindavana, the darshana on four sides of Sri Rama, Sri Narasimha, Sri Krishna and Sri Vedavyasa. This sacred vision is reproduced on the four sides of the Brindavana gopuram.

While gopuram darshana may be obtained elsewhere, circumambulation around the gopuram is a special feature here. Flying above is the Dvaraka flag. At Dvaraka the flag is raised five times each day; here it is changed five times each year.

title: Sri Nijarupa Raghavendra
summary: A lifelike Sri Raghavendra sits eight feet below the Brindavana, as He is believed to remain at Mantralayam, contemplating seventy-two forms of Bhagavan.
body:
In 1671 at Mantralayam, Sri Raghavendra entered the earth alive, declaring that He would remain for a further seven hundred years. Eight feet beneath the original Brindavana, unseen by our eyes, He remains in prayer for us, meditating upon seventy-two forms of Bhagavan and the attendant deities.

With this as the model, Sri Nijarupa Raghavendra sits eight feet below the Brindavana at Granthalaya. The figure is called Nijarupa because it was sculpted from descriptions of how Sri Raghavendra appeared in His own lifetime, and its radiant lifelikeness feels almost like beholding Him in person.

Devotees who circumambulate Sri Nijarupa Rayaru twelve times also circumambulate the seventy-two forms He worships, receiving together the grace of the deities and Guru Raja.

title: Sri Aishvarya Vinayaka and the Neem Tree
summary: A right-trunked Ganapati consecrated before any construction began, beside a neem tree that had sprung up of its own accord.
body:
This right-trunked Aishvarya Vinayaka came through Nandagokulam of Gobichettipalayam. After the bhoomi puja on 8 May 2011, when no buildings yet stood, a vastu expert directed that a neem sapling be planted and Ganapati consecrated in a particular southwestern corner before construction began. When the weeds were cleared at that precise spot, a neem tree had already sprung up naturally and grown two feet tall.

Sri Aishvarya Vinayaka was consecrated there on 24 April 2012. Only then did the other work proceed, leading to the Kumbhabhishekam of 9 February 2017.
images: SRI AISHVARYA VINAYAKA AND THE NEEM TREE.jpg

title: The Rare Naga Images of Bikshalaya
summary: Two naturally formed stone Nagas from Bikshalaya, the native place of Appannacharya, consecrated beside a self-grown peepal tree.
body:
Bikshalaya is a village about twenty kilometres from Mantralayam, on the opposite bank of the Tungabhadra. It is the native place of Appannacharya, Sri Raghavendra's most devoted disciple, and is revered as a realm of Nagas. Thousands of naturally occurring stone Naga images are believed to lie buried there.

Two such images emerged in September 2016 and were brought to Granthalaya. In August 2017, before Sri Raghavendra's aradhana, they were consecrated beside a peepal tree that had grown of its own accord. Devotees regard circumambulation of these Nagas as beneficial for astrological remedies.
images: THE RARE NAGA IMAGES OF BIKSHALAYA.jpg

title: The Sacred Sandalwood-Grinding Stone
summary: The stone on which Venkatanatha ground sandalwood while reciting the Agni and Varuna Suktas, now in the sanctum.
body:
In His earlier life, when Sri Raghavendra was Venkatanatha, He came to Tirukkattupalli seeking a means to support His family. At a house holding a samaradhana, He worshipped the presiding deity Sri Agnishvara and was asked to grind sandalwood paste. Meditating on the deity, He recited the Agni Sukta while grinding, and those who applied the paste developed painful blisters. He then sanctified the remaining paste with the Varuna Sukta, and their bodies became well again. The incident dates to around 1616-1617.

The grinding stone connected with this event reached Granthalaya on 12 May 2019 and now holds a place of honour in the sanctum. Devotees believe that beholding it brings relief from afflictions of body and mind.

title: The Holy Sivalinga Worshipped by the Kanchi Paramacharya
summary: Facing Sri Avatara Traya Hanuman, as at Mantralayam, a Sivalinga once worshipped by the Sage of Kanchi.
body:
At Mantralayam, Sri Hanuman stands opposite Sri Raghavendra, and beside Hanuman is a Sivalinga worshipped by Sri Raghavendra. In this way Sri Raghavendra shows the importance of revering Lord Siva, the presiding deity of knowledge.

At Granthalaya, the replica of Mantralayam, Sri Avatara Traya Hanuman similarly faces the Brindavana, with a Sivalinga nearby. This very Sivalinga was worshipped by the Kanchi Paramacharya. It is revered as possessing the sanctity of Kashi, and its history is told in volume twelve of Sri Raghavendra Mahimai.
images: HOLY SIVALINGA WORSHIPPED BY THE KANCHI PARAMACHARYA.jpg

title: Sri Shankukarna, the Original Form of Sri Raghavendra
summary: A flower-filled shrine to the primordial form of Sri Raghavendra, a rare darshana not readily found even at Mantralayam.
body:
In Brahmaloka, Sri Shankukarna brought flowers daily for the worship of Sri Narayana. One day He was delayed, and Brahma pronounced a boon disguised as a curse: "You shall be born upon earth!"

Shankukarna incarnated as Sri Prahlada in Krita Yuga, King Bahlika in Dvapara Yuga, and Sri Vyasaraja and Sri Raghavendra in Kali Yuga. Granthalaya has created a lovely, flower-filled, separate shrine to Sri Shankukarna. The devotional belief is that darshana of Shankukarna brings the merit of beholding all His incarnations.

title: Sri Varaha Swami, the Tungabhadra and Srimad Appannacharya
summary: The birth of the Tunga and Bhadra from Lord Varaha's tusks, recreated in black stone, and Appannacharya's rush to the Brindavana.
body:
The Tungabhadra has its source in the Sahyadri mountains. According to tradition, when Lord Varaha rested there after raising the earth, the Tunga issued from one tusk and the Bhadra from the other. They met at Kudali, became the Tungabhadra and joined the Krishna near Kurnool. Water from the Krishna reaches Poondi Reservoir through the Telugu Ganga scheme, and since Granthalaya lies below this reservoir, its setting evokes Mantralayam. Here the Sahyadri, a huge image of Lord Varaha and the birth of the two rivers have been recreated in black stone.

When Sri Raghavendra entered the Brindavana in 1671, Srimad Appannacharya hurried from Bikshalaya singing the Sri Raghavendra Guru Stotram, and the Tungabhadra is said to have parted to allow him passage. This scene is recreated before the Brindavana, with a magnificent six-foot stone image of Appannacharya.

title: Kalpavriksha, Kamadhenu, the Feet of Sri Raghavendra and the Great Chariot
summary: A stone Kalpavriksha, a marble Kamadhenu, the sacred feet for abhisheka and archana, and the grand temple chariot.
body:
In the verse beginning "Pujyaya Raghavendraya," Srimad Appannacharya compares Sri Raghavendra to the wish-fulfilling Kalpavriksha and Kamadhenu. Here, before Sri Nijarupa Raghavendra, devotees can behold a Kalpavriksha carved in stone and a Kamadhenu fashioned from marble.

The sacred feet of Sri Raghavendra are also installed so that devotees may themselves perform abhisheka and archana. With the arrival of the grand temple chariot, many more wonders and lifelike sacred representations await.
